newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PORT OF ROTTERDAM AND GERMAN ARG IN PIPELINE J-V.
newsitem.headline: PORT OF ROTTERDAM AND GERMAN ARG IN PIPELINE J-V.

text.p: The Port of Rotterdam and German firm Aethylen Rohrleitungs Gesellschaft (ARG) have signed a letter of intent on a 50/50 joint venture to build a pipeline linking Antwerp with Rotterdam, the port said on Wednesday.
The pipeline will be about 115 kilometers long and will come into operation in the middle of 1999 at a total cost of some 80 million guilders.
The pipeline will transport ethylene and will be a common carrier pipeline (CPPS), meaning it can be used by any company subject to a number of transport conditions, the statement said.
"By opening pipelines to third parties, the Port (of Rotterdam) intends to create an extra stimulus for the activity in the chemicals port," the statement said.
Arco Chemicals will be the first company using the pipeline.

"To ARG, the CPPS is an important addition to its common carrier ethylene transportation network linking the Ruhr area, Antwerp and Limburg (in southern Netherlands) and totalling 490 kilometres," the statement said.
ARG is a transport company which operates ethylene pipelines for DSM and five German chemical firms.
